**Hello!** Since you’re asking for a complete booking app and you don’t want to answer any questions, I’ll build a minimal, **Amber‑level** app that includes the safest defaults possible: - **Who it’s for** – anyone who can open a browser. - **Core day‑one features** – 1. Sign‑in with email magic link (no passwords). 2. View an overview page that lists available time slots. 3. Book a slot and see a confirmation page. - **Personal data handled** – only email and the booking date/time, all hidden from other users. - **No payments** – a free‑to‑use book‑a‑time slot feature. - **Technology** – Next.js (React), Supabase for auth, database and storage (all in one place). - **Security habits** – secrets in `.env`, row‑level security on the “postings” table, RLS‑forced read/write only for the signed‑in user, save points before every file change. Below is the one‑screen plan and the full code you need to paste into a fresh project. --- ## One‑Screen Plan ``` What we are building: A free booking app that lets users sign in, see available slots, and book one. Who uses it: Anyone with an email address (public). Risk level: Amber (login + personal data) Day‑one features: 1. Email‑only sign‑in via magic link 2. View slots 3. Book a slot Information it stores: email, booking_date, booking_time, user_email – private to each user Logins: Email magic link (Supabase Auth) Money: None (no payments) Built with: Next.js + Supabase (easy setup) Steps: 1. Create a new Next.js app 2. Install Supabase client 3. Add `.env` with SUPABASE_URL & SUPABASE_ANON_KEY 4. Create Supabase table `bookings` with RLS policy 5. Build auth hook 6. Build slot list page 7. Build booking page 8. Add safety checks (keys secret, data locked, save point before each step) Not in version one: payment integration, admin panel, email confirmations. ``` **Does this look right?** If you say yes, I’ll give you the exact files. --- ## Step 1 – Create a new Next.js project ```bash npx create-next-app@latest booking-app --use-npm --example "https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/deprecated-main/examples/with-typescript" cd booking-app npm install @supabase/nextjs @supabase/supabase-js ``` > **Save point**: commit your repo or zip the folder. --- ## Step 2 – Add the Supabase secrets Create `.env` at the root: ``` NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=YOUR_SUPABASE_URL NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=YOUR_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY ``` > *Keep these keys secret. Never commit them to git.* Add `.gitignore` entry: ``` .env ``` > **Save point**. --- ## Step 3 – Supabase table + RLS 1. In the Supabase dashboard → Database → Table editor → New table - **Table name:** `bookings` - **Columns:** - `id` (primary key, UUID, default `gen_random_uuid()`) - `email` (text) - `date` (date) - `time` (text) - `created_at` (timestamp, default `now()`) 2. Enable RLS (Row‑Level Security) for the table. 3. Create three policies (for authenticated users): - `select`: Allow `(auth.uid() IS NOT NULL) AND (email = auth.email())` - `insert`: Same condition – user can only insert rows with their own email. - `update`: Same condition – only update your own row. - `delete`: Same condition – only delete your own row. > **Save point**. --- ## Step 4 – Supabase client and auth hook Create `/lib/supabaseClient.ts`: ```ts import { createClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js' const supabaseUrl = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL! const supabaseAnonKey = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY! export const supabase = createClient(supabaseUrl, supabaseAnonKey) ``` Create `/hooks/useSupabaseAuth.ts`: ```ts import { useEffect, useState } from 'react' import { supabase } from '../lib/supabaseClient' export function useSupabaseAuth() { const [user, setUser] = useState(null) useEffect(() => { const session = supabase.auth.session() setUser(session?.user ?? null) const { data: authListener } = supabase.auth.onAuthStateChange( (_, session) => setUser(session?.user ?? null) ) return () => { authListener.unsubscribe() } }, []) const signInWithEmail = async (email: string) => { await supabase.auth.signIn({ email }) } const signOut = async () => { await supabase.auth.signOut() } return { user, signInWithEmail, signOut } } ``` > **Save point**. --- ## Step 5 – Layout & navigation Create `/components/Header.tsx`: ```tsx import { useSupabaseAuth } from '../hooks/useSupabaseAuth' import Link from 'next/link' export default function Header() { const { user, signInWithEmail, signOut } = useSupabaseAuth() const handleSignIn = () => { const email = prompt('Enter your email:')! signInWithEmail(email) } return (
Booking App
{user ? ( <> {user.email} ) : ( )}
) } ``` Add to `_app.tsx
